chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the Imam: does he know the unseen? So he said: “No; rather, when he intends to know a thing, Allah informs him of that.”

key_terms.أَرَادَ: intended or willed, indicating the Imam’s wish to know
key_terms.أَعْلَمَهُ: He informed him, meaning Allah caused him to know
key_terms.الشَّيْءَ: a thing, meaning a particular matter or reality
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who grants such knowledge
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader being asked about
key_terms.الْغَيْبَ: the unseen, hidden realities not accessible through ordinary means

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam عليه السلام know the unseen independently?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the Imam’s knowledge of the unseen and clarifies that independent knowledge of al-ghayb is not affirmed here. Rather, when the Imam wishes to know something, Allah grants him that knowledge.
